stemBlocks.value: Three triangles are drawn on a square grid: X with vertices (0, 2), (6, 2), (4, 4); Y with vertices (0, −2), (6, −2), (4, −4); Z with vertices (−2, 0), (−2, 6), (−4, 4). (i) X is mapped onto Y by a reflection — state the equation of the mirror line. (ii) Describe fully the transformation which maps X onto Z. (iii) Translate Y using the vector (−7, 1) and label the image V. (iv) Enlarge X about the centre C(0, 0) by scale factor 1/2 and label the image W.
Think first: Write down the vertices of all three triangles first; every part is then a comparison of coordinates.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p257-q16 from workbook page 257.

solutionSteps.instruction: Compare X with Y vertex by vertex.

contentBlocks.value: (0, 2) → (0, −2), (6, 2) → (6, −2), (4, 4) → (4, −4): the x-coordinates are unchanged and the y-coordinates change sign
Result: Reflection in the x-axis, y = 0

solutionSteps.instruction: Compare X with Z vertex by vertex.

contentBlocks.value: Result: A quarter turn anticlockwise about the origin

solutionSteps.instruction: State the transformation for X onto Z in full.

contentBlocks.value: Type, angle, direction and centre are all required

solutionSteps.instruction: Enlarge X about the origin by scale factor 1/2.

strategyBlocks.value: Match each vertex of X with its partner in Y and in Z to identify the mirror line and the rotation, then apply the given vector and scale factor to produce V and W.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) The mirror line is the x-axis, y = 0.  (ii) A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin (0, 0).  (iii) Triangle V has vertices (−7, −1), (−1, −1) and (−3, −3).  (iv) Triangle W has vertices (0, 1), (3, 1) and (2, 2).

whyThisWorks.value: Each transformation leaves a fingerprint in the coordinates: a reflection in the x-axis keeps x and negates y; a 90° anticlockwise rotation about the origin sends (x, y) to (−y, x); a translation adds a fixed vector to every point; and an enlargement about the origin multiplies every coordinate by the scale factor. Checking the rule on all three vertices, not just one, is what proves the description is correct.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the mirror line as 'the x-axis' without the equation y = 0, or writing x = 0.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the mirror line as 'the x-axis' without the equation y = 0, or writing x = 0.

commonErrors.misconception: Stating the rotation as clockwise, or omitting the centre.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stating the rotation as clockwise, or omitting the centre.

commonErrors.misconception: Applying the translation vector to the wrong triangle (X instead of Y).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Applying the translation vector to the wrong triangle (X instead of Y).

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying coordinates by 2 instead of 1/2 for the enlargement.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying coordinates by 2 instead of 1/2 for the enlargement.

examTip.value: Test any suspected rule on every vertex — a rule that works for one point can easily be the wrong transformation.
